root.title: Own the composition and long-lived gateway, while reusing DSH runtime primitives.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The gateway, deployment composition, event-sourced turn path, and evidence boundaries below each hold.

sections.label: When
sections.body: Firstmate receives consecutive prompts in one named session.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: One coherent Firstmate conversation uses DSH primitives without making agent-spine-demo the process entry or the complete harness.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The current proof establishes continuity in one subprocess lifetime. Interactive intake, cold resume, and compaction each remain separately verifiable work.

children.title: One gateway owns identity, session, and subprocess lifecycle.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The command admits credentials, opens one reusable SDK runtime, and the runtime owns its child process.

sections.label: When
sections.body: A person starts Firstmate and sends sequential prompts to one named session.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The conversation stays coherent for the subprocess lifetime and tears down cleanly when the gateway closes.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: This is the Agent-Neo ownership seam. It keeps the human in one terminal while DSH remains a reusable runtime dependency.

children.title: The command entry selects one explicit path.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Credential admission and the reusable runtime are available.

sections.label: When
sections.body: main() receives demo or live through process.argv.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: demo runs the deterministic scenario, live runs a live turn, and an unknown command fails explicitly.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The live route currently accepts one argv prompt then exits. It is not yet the desired interactive terminal loop.

children.title: Credential admission keeps the secret outside configuration and output.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Either DEEPSEEK_API_KEY exists or stdin and stderr are interactive terminals.

sections.label: When
sections.body: acquireLiveDeepSeekConnection() is called.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It returns the key with the official base URL, avoids prompting when an environment key exists, and otherwise reads without echoing.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The secret travels only through the child environment, never through JSON-RPC or cordis.yml.

children.title: The Firstmate wrapper owns one reusable SDK runtime.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The SDK can start and the caller supplies credential, session root, workspace root, and model limits.

sections.label: When
sections.body: openFirstmateRuntime() is called.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: One DeepSeekHarness is reused across named-session runs, and close() owns complete teardown.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: A persistent terminal Firstmate retains this returned object across prompts.

children.title: The high-level SDK owns one complete activity interval.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The JSON-RPC client can start the configured executable.

sections.label: When
sections.body: HarnessSession.run() receives content for a session ID.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It initializes lazily, subscribes before prompting, waits for inbox receipt and the next idle state, then returns the response and events.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: DeepSeekHarness.start() memoizes initialization, so repeated runs reuse one child until close.

children.title: HarnessClient is the OS-level parent of DSH.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The child runner can boot the selected configuration and the executable can start.

sections.label: When
sections.body: HarnessClient.start() runs.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It spawns the child with piped stdio, exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC, fans out notifications, retains stderr diagnostics, and reaps the child on close.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: This client lives outside Cordis. It creates the harness process itself.

children.title: The child runner owns DSH process startup and shutdown.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: A valid configuration path is supplied.

sections.label: When
sections.body: packaged-bin.ts calls runJsonrpcAgent().

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The selected configuration boots, EOF and signals dispose the context, and no fallback configuration hides a missing file.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The packaged bin supplies the bare-module resolution base. The runner owns signals and exit behavior.

children.title: Cordis composition determines what the harness actually contains.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The loader can resolve the root configuration and each enabled extension has its declared dependencies.

sections.label: When
sections.body: DSH boots the Firstmate configuration.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The SDK server, DeepSeek adapter, common spine, persistence, checkpoint policy, token meter, and compaction engine mount as an intentional deployment.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The spine is a nested convenience bundle, not the deployment owner. Agent-Neo should own composition under mine/.

children.title: Boot waits until the complete plugin tree is ready.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Every configured plugin resolves.

sections.label: When
sections.body: boot() installs the Cordis Loader and mounts the root include.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: Every entry is imported, schema-normalized, mounted, and active before readiness is advertised.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: File order is not dependency order. Cordis keeps plugins pending until declared injected services exist.

children.title: cordis.yml defines the concrete Firstmate deployment.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Every enabled sibling can activate and each disabled capability remains absent.

sections.label: When
sections.body: The Loader reads the prototype cordis.yml.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The runtime contains the SDK server, DeepSeek adapter, agent spine, JSONL persistence, checkpoint policy, token meter, and compaction engine.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: Skills, Bash, workspace context, goals, and model-facing job controls are explicitly disabled.

children.title: The JSON-RPC server turns wire prompts into agent inbox messages.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The registry and concrete loop factory are available.

sections.label: When
sections.body: HarnessSdkJsonRpcServer.prompt() receives session/prompt.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It finds or creates one agent, converts content blocks into a user message, calls followup(), and returns the durable message ID.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: Unknown session IDs always land in ctx.agents.create(). The server does not select the separately available resume path.

children.title: agent-spine-demo assembles common services but does not own the deployment.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Its required child services can mount.

sections.label: When
sections.body: agent-spine-demo.apply() receives its Cordis context and configuration.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It mounts common services, forwards each configuration field to its owner, and omits optional capabilities configured as false.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: This is the replacement seam for an owned composition under mine/. It is a convenience bundle, not the minimum DSH agent.

children.title: The registry owns agent identity while the loop owns behavior.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The loop has registered itself as the active factory.

sections.label: When
sections.body: AgentRegistry.create() receives a session ID and agent options.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It delegates construction to the factory, publishes one live agent and session, and returns an owned disposal handle.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The registry provides creation, lookup, lineage, and lifecycle ownership. It does not implement model turns.

children.title: AgentLoop is the factory for the concrete turn machine.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Session, LLM, tools, system prompt, and agent services exist.

sections.label: When
sections.body: AgentLoop.createAgent() is called.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It prepares a session, constructs ReactLoopAgent, installs rollback-safe lifecycle ownership, publishes both identities, and returns a handle.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: AgentLoop.resume() already exists. Cold resume fails higher up because the SDK server never calls it.

children.title: An event-sourced turn pipeline connects human input to DeepSeek and back.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: A user message reaches an idle agent and the Firstmate persona, provider transport, and durability policy are configured.

sections.label: When
sections.body: ReactLoopAgent.followup() wakes the agent.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The runtime derives history from canonical events, makes one model request, records the response, and returns to idle with durable session history.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The session log is the shared state boundary for prompts, events, persistence, metering, and compaction.

children.title: ReactLoopAgent converts inbox work into canonical turn events.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Prompt assembly, provider transport, and durability boundaries hold, and the inbox receives a user message.

sections.label: When
sections.body: ReactLoopAgent.followup() wakes an idle agent.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The agent records turn and step boundaries, derives history, performs the request, records the assistant response, and returns to idle.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: turn() owns boundaries, step() owns streaming and tools, and buildRequest() freezes the provider request.

children.title: Prompt assembly exposes identity without exposing unwanted authority.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The Firstmate persona is configured and model-facing capability providers are disabled.

sections.label: When
sections.body: SystemPrompt.assemble() runs before a model step.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The rendered system prompt contains Firstmate identity while the assembled tool list is empty.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: ToolRuntime remains infrastructure. An empty registry is different from removing the execution service.

children.title: The DeepSeek adapter owns only provider transport.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The LLM request has a route, messages, credential, endpoint, and cancellation signal.

sections.label: When
sections.body: DeepSeekAdapter.stream() is invoked.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It serializes chat completions, sends HTTPS, parses SSE, emits DSH chunks, and normalizes provider and transport errors.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The deterministic gate exercised the real adapter against a local provider substitute. A previous external DeepSeek call is recorded separately.

children.title: Semantic checkpoints make the event log durable before side effects.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: A live session emits canonical events, JSONL persistence is mounted, and checkpoint policy is active.

sections.label: When
sections.body: The agent reaches a model, tool, step, or teardown durability boundary.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: All prior events flush before the side effect proceeds, and the backend writes them to the session artifact.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The session log is the source of truth for assistant chunks, messages, request headers, boundaries, and tool results.

children.title: Compaction should replace old surface only after measured pressure requires it.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The token meter can replay the session, the adapter reports context capacity, and pressure crosses the configured threshold.

sections.label: When
sections.body: BasicCompactionEngine.compactIfNeeded() runs at the next pre-step boundary.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: It selects a safe old region, summarizes it, records a durable replacement, retains the recent tail, and remeasures below threshold.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: The short scenario mounts this component but never reaches 80 percent pressure. A focused long-transcript proof is still required.

children.title: The current evidence establishes a useful boundary and makes remaining gaps explicit.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: Same-process continuity, Firstmate identity, empty model-facing tools, JSONL durability, and the local adapter substitute all have evidence.

sections.label: When
sections.body: The prototype is assessed against the intended long-lived Firstmate experience.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The accepted boundary is clear: one-runtime continuity works now, while interactive intake, cold resume, and triggered compaction remain unproven.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: Treating these as distinct proofs prevents a strong same-process demo from silently claiming a complete harness.

children.title: The deterministic scenario proves same-process continuity and durable output.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: One runtime is retained and both prompts use the same session ID.

sections.label: When
sections.body: runPrototypeScenario() sends two sequential prompts before closing the runtime.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: Two model requests occur, the second contains the first prompt, Firstmate identity is present, model-facing tools are empty, and session.jsonl exists.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: bun run verify passed this closest-substitute proof. It does not prove cold resume after restart.

children.title: A long-lived terminal loop is the next proof for human input.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: The gateway, deployment, and turn pipeline hold, and stdin supplies two prompts followed by /exit.

sections.label: When
sections.body: One terminal command starts Firstmate.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: Both prompts use one runtime and session, output remains concise, and exit flushes JSONL before the child terminates.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: This closes the human-input landing gap without mixing in cold resume or worker delegation.

children.title: Cold resume needs a resume-aware SDK server decision.

sections.label: Given
sections.body: A durable session exists and a fresh runtime receives its ID.

sections.label: When
sections.body: The first prompt reaches the new server process.

sections.label: Expect
sections.body: The server selects ctx.agents.resume(), restores history, and performs the next model step without an identity collision.

sections.label: Notes
sections.body: This needs a thin Agent-Neo adapter or an upstream SDK change. It follows the multi-turn live proof.
